subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Engine Cooling
description: Learn Engine Cooling in one minute.

hook.text: Burning fuel inside an engine creates temperatures over 2,000°F. Without cooling, it would melt.

buildup.text: Most cars pump coolant through channels in the engine block to absorb heat and carry it away.

discovery.text: The hot coolant flows to the radiator, where air passing through thin fins cools it back down.

twist.text: A thermostat blocks coolant flow when the engine is cold—engines need warmth to run efficiently.

climax.text: If the system fails, the engine overheats in minutes. That's why the temperature gauge matters.

punchline.text: Engines are controlled explosions kept cool by plumbing.
